item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-2300c3d3c033cc4f","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"During the review period, policymaking was dominated by the military and intelligence agencies; presidential powers were extensive, judicial independence was severely restricted, and parliament functioned largely as a pro-regime rubber stamp.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.5","8B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report covers the period leading into 2023 and is materially relevant to the 2023 institutional context.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes these institutional conditions to President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's regime.","limitations":["Institutional findings are presented as an expert country assessment rather than a quantified 2023 measurement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2300c3d3c033cc4f","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The government published a national human rights strategy, established a presidential amnesty committee, initiated a national dialogue, and allowed the state of emergency to expire; the report found that these measures produced no significant results during the review period.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.9","4B.3","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report describes measures and results relevant to the 2023 period, while noting some initiatives began earlier.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the measures to Sisi and his government.","limitations":["The report does not provide a complete list of releases or implementation milestones."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2300c3d3c033cc4f","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The regime continued heavy repression; civil society was harshly restricted, political prisoners numbered in the tens of thousands, forced disappearance and torture were described as widespread, and media remained under strict state control.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding concerns the report's review period, which includes the 2023 context.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the repression to the regime under Sisi.","limitations":["The prisoner figure is expressed broadly as “tens of thousands.”"]},{"source_id":"SRC-2300c3d3c033cc4f","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Economic output and fiscal and monetary stability weakened, with depleted foreign-currency reserves, high inflation, rising debt, and increasing interest payments; austerity, including subsidy cuts and reduced education and health spending, increased poverty and eroded the middle class.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report describes economic conditions during the period under review, including effects continuing into 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the policies and fiscal choices to Sisi's government.","limitations":["The report identifies COVID-19 and the Ukraine war as external shocks affecting outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-97452a456e06a242","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Egypt approved a 2022–2026 anti-trafficking strategy, increased convictions, more than doubled training, and issued presidential directives prioritizing awareness and victim protection; nevertheless, victim identification and investigations declined, services and shelters remained insufficient, and Egypt was downgraded to Tier 2 Watch List.","question_ids":["3B.7","5B.6","6B.3","6B.4","6B.6","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report covers April 2022 to March 2023 and directly overlaps the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the directives and government actions to Egypt's government and president.","limitations":["Most quantitative prosecution data reported are for calendar year 2022 rather than all of 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-97452a456e06a242","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The government identified 212 trafficking victims in 2022, down from 272 in 2021 and 519 in 2020; almost all identified victims were Egyptian, while services for foreign and male victims remained limited.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The figures are 2022 results reported in a report covering the first quarter of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The finding concerns government identification and referral practices.","limitations":["The source notes that inconsistent identification may mean actual victimization was higher."]},{"source_id":"SRC-97452a456e06a242","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Egypt maintained specialized prosecution offices, judicial circuits, and trained more than 2,100 officials and NGO partners through over 70 anti-trafficking sessions; observers nevertheless reported inconsistent use of victim-identification procedures and inadequate services.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.4","5B.2","6B.4","8B.3","8B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The training and institutional findings concern the reporting period ending in March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the measures to the Prosecutor General's Office, Ministry of Justice, and national anti-trafficking committee.","limitations":["Training activity is evidence of institutional effort, not proof of effective victim outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-832c0164537b73cd","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Freedom House rated Egypt Not Free with a global freedom score of 18/100; it found meaningful opposition virtually nonexistent, dissent criminalized, civil liberties tightly restricted, and security-force abuses occurring with impunity.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.8","4B.1","4B.3","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The 2023 country report primarily assesses conditions in 2022 but describes the governing environment entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the pattern to Sisi's increasingly authoritarian rule.","limitations":["The report's score is not a measurement limited strictly to calendar year 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-832c0164537b73cd","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Freedom House found that Sisi's 2018 election was noncompetitive, with opposition candidates pressured to withdraw, state resources and media supporting his candidacy, intimidation, vote buying, and low turnout; 2019 amendments extended his current term through 2024 and allowed an additional six-year term.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"These are institutional facts inherited into the 2023 period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the constitutional amendments and electoral advantage to Sisi's regime.","limitations":["The election and amendments predate 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-832c0164537b73cd","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The president and security apparatus dominated policymaking; parliament lacked a meaningful checking role, and public spending and military-business finances were largely opaque, including inaccessible state-owned-enterprise debt and unpublished military-enterprise audits.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.6","5B.5","5B.7","7B.6","7B.7","8B.3","8B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report describes the governing structure and transparency conditions entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes executive dominance and opacity to Sisi and the security apparatus.","limitations":["The report does not quantify all military-linked expenditures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-832c0164537b73cd","start_unit":8,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The media sector was dominated by progovernment outlets; critical outlets were shut down, online censorship could occur without judicial approval, hundreds of websites had been blocked, and activists, journalists, and content creators faced surveillance, arrest, and prosecution for dissenting expression.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report assesses conditions in 2022 and the continuing framework relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes censorship and surveillance to Egyptian authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["The website and journalist figures are mainly for periods before or during 2022."]},{"source_id":"SRC-832c0164537b73cd","start_unit":11,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"Executive influence over courts, prolonged pretrial detention, military jurisdiction over civilians, poor prison conditions, torture allegations, deaths in custody, discrimination, and weak enforcement against gender-based violence were documented as continuing features of governance.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","4B.4","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report summarizes conditions inherited into 2023, including examples from 2021–2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report links the judicial and security framework to constitutional and executive changes under Sisi.","limitations":["Several examples predate 2023 and are contextual rather than 2023 events."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7007786c0db638ef","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"During the first quarter of 2023, AFTE recorded 31 freedom-of-expression violations; the presidential pardon committee's releases were slow and selective, while arrests and prosecutions of opinion holders continued at a greater rate than releases.","question_ids":["3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 1 January–31 March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"AFTE attributes the release process and continuing arrests to state and security authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["AFTE's count reflects documented cases and may not capture all incidents."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7007786c0db638ef","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Three Mada Masr journalists were referred to an economic court in February 2023 over a report about alleged financial violations by leaders of the pro-government Mostaqbal Watan Party; the site's licensing application had remained unanswered since 2020.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The prosecutions and licensing status were reported during the first quarter of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The fact concerns judicial and media-regulatory authorities operating under the government.","limitations":["The underlying financial allegations were reported as allegations, not established findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7007786c0db638ef","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Security authorities arrested people in January–February 2023 for Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, or other videos and posts criticizing prices, currency depreciation, police detention, or political conditions; charges included terrorism, false news, and misuse of social media, with prolonged pretrial detention.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers incidents in the first quarter of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"AFTE attributes the arrests and prosecutions to security forces and State Security Prosecution.","limitations":["The cases are individually documented incidents and do not establish the total number of such arrests."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7007786c0db638ef","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"On 15 January 2023, an emergency terrorism court imposed lengthy prison sentences on defendants in the 'Joker' case; AFTE reported random arrests, torture allegations, fabricated evidence, delayed investigations, and lack of fair trials.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The judgment and reported procedural concerns occurred or were documented in the first quarter of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The case involved emergency-court and security authorities under the Sisi government.","limitations":["The source is an NGO monitoring report and reports allegations concerning trial conduct."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7007786c0db638ef","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"In February 2023, a university referred a student to investigation over a supposedly blasphemous social-media post; an inquiry reportedly found her account had been hacked and she was not responsible, while an academic was again investigated and another academic's salary was stopped over travel during leave.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.5"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers incidents in February 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The actions were taken by university and security-linked authorities within the state system.","limitations":["The student case includes a reported exculpatory finding by the inquiry; the source does not provide an independent court determination."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7b0ffaa93410531b","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"During the 2023 presidential-election endorsement phase, only 217 notary offices were allocated compared with 389 in 2018; campaigners reported blocked access, assaults, intimidation, malfunctioning registration systems, political-money inducements, and at least 140 arrests of Ahmed al-Tantawy campaign members.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.9","7B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers the July–September 2023 pre-election period.","ruler_attribution":"AFTE attributes the restrictions, arrests, and non-response to the National Election Authority, security forces, and authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["Some assaults were attributed to unidentified civilian-clothed persons; AFTE reports police non-intervention."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7b0ffaa93410531b","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Citizen Lab reported that presidential hopeful Ahmed al-Tantawy's phone was targeted with Predator spyware using a zero-day exploit; because Egypt was a known client and one attempt originated inside Egypt, Citizen Lab assessed with high confidence that the Egyptian government was responsible.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The finding was reported during the September 2023 election period.","ruler_attribution":"The attribution is Citizen Lab's high-confidence assessment, not a judicial finding.","limitations":["The source reports an external technical attribution rather than a publicly acknowledged government order."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7b0ffaa93410531b","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"In August–September 2023, authorities arrested or prosecuted people for criticizing Sisi's candidacy or supporting an opposition candidate, including a police officer and a man who posted a video criticizing a third term; both were detained on terrorism or false-news charges.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.8","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers incidents in the third quarter of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"AFTE attributes the arrests to security forces and State Security Prosecution.","limitations":["The source reports charges and detention, not final convictions in these particular cases."]},{"source_id":"SRC-7b0ffaa93410531b","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"During the third quarter of 2023, authorities and affiliated media or regulatory bodies arrested a journalist, removed or truncated political interviews and articles, disrupted an independent news website, deleted content, and referred a television presenter to investigation over a personal Facebook post.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly covers July–September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"AFTE attributes the pattern to Egyptian authorities, security forces, and state-linked media institutions.","limitations":["Some incidents were attributed to unnamed parties or corporate decisions rather than a formally identified presidential order."]},{"source_id":"SRC-72828bb1a437d741","start_unit":13,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The study found that Egyptian higher-education reform combined privatization, user fees, cost sharing, and quality assurance with the exclusion of academic freedom, university autonomy, and equitable access; accreditation was often reduced to administrative paperwork and did not reliably indicate educational quality.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.6","6B.2","6B.5","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Published in 2023 but analyzes reforms over a longer period; relevant as an institutional finding entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The study attributes the reform trajectory to Egyptian governments and World Bank-supported policy transfer, not solely to Sisi personally.","limitations":["The analysis is historical and theoretical rather than a year-specific evaluation of 2023 implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-72828bb1a437d741","start_unit":16,"end_unit":18,"fact_summary":"The study reports that post-2013 authorities reversed earlier university autonomy gains, restored presidential appointment of university leaders, controlled student elections, required security clearance for academic travel, and left higher-education access biased toward wealthier and urban groups.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.5","4B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The findings describe the institutional condition carried into 2023, based on developments since 2013.","ruler_attribution":"The study attributes the reversal to the government after the military return to power and the Sisi era.","limitations":["The access statistics cited are from earlier studies and are not 2023 outcome measurements."]},{"source_id":"SRC-551e29fd645cf841","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Egyptian Taskforce reported that human-rights conditions remained unaddressed three years after Egypt accepted 288 of 375 UPR recommendations; it characterized state initiatives, including the national strategy, pardon committee, and national dialogue, as symbolic and found torture, disappearance, arbitrary detention, and judicial complicity persisted.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","7B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published January 2023 and assesses implementation through the end of 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the policies and institutional failures to Egyptian authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["This is a coalition NGO assessment and uses a broad systemic characterization."]},{"source_id":"SRC-551e29fd645cf841","start_unit":11,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The report documented routine indefinite pretrial-detention renewals, erosion of judicial independence, expansion of military jurisdiction over civilians, acceptance of torture-tainted proceedings, recycling of detainees into new cases, and broad use of terrorism and false-news charges against peaceful expression.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was issued in January 2023 and summarizes documented practices through 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report links the legal changes and executive authority to the Sisi government.","limitations":["Several quantitative examples concern 2020–2022 rather than calendar year 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-551e29fd645cf841","start_unit":18,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"The report stated that anti-cybercrime and communications laws enabled broad surveillance, required providers to retain user data for 180 days, and supported blocking at least 600 websites, including press, human-rights, opposition, VPN, and social-media sites.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in January 2023 and describes the legal and censorship framework entering the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the surveillance and blocking powers to Egyptian security and regulatory authorities.","limitations":["The website count was compiled from earlier reporting and is not necessarily a 2023-only count."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e82050a082d661af","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In 2023, President Sisi pardoned Patrick Zaki one day after an emergency court sentenced him to three years for a 2019 article about discrimination against Copts; the pardon also lifted his travel ban.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","7B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers July 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The pardon and travel-ban lifting were ordered by President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.","limitations":["The pardon corrected an individual case but does not establish broader institutional reform."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e82050a082d661af","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In 2023, authorities detained or prosecuted people for religious expression, including a TikTok creator sentenced to three years for insulting Christianity and a Quranist activist prevented from travelling without a judicial order; a university investigation into an allegedly blasphemous post was closed after a hacking claim.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers 2023 incidents.","ruler_attribution":"The detentions, prosecution, travel restriction, and university response involved Egyptian judicial, security, and administrative authorities.","limitations":["The source records allegations and official actions but does not resolve the factual truth of the disputed online posts."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e82050a082d661af","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The government legalized 141 churches and 233 connected properties in June 2023, bringing the total legalized to 2,973 of 3,730 pending requests; it also restored religious sites and inaugurated a large Islamic Cultural Center, while Shia Muslims remained unable to establish public places of worship.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers government actions and religious-freedom conditions in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Church legalization and major religious-site projects were undertaken by the government under Sisi; restrictions on Shia worship remained state policy or practice.","limitations":["Legalization figures do not demonstrate equal treatment across all religious groups."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e82050a082d661af","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The government continued using customary reconciliation in sectarian disputes; human-rights and Christian representatives said such sessions pressured Christians to retract statements and sometimes replaced criminal proceedings, while the constitutionally mandated independent anti-discrimination commission had still not been established.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","4B.4","4B.7","6B.8","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report describes practices and institutional omissions during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The reconciliation system and failure to establish the commission concern state institutions under Sisi.","limitations":["Some criticisms come from civil-society and community representatives rather than a court finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e82050a082d661af","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"President Sisi reiterated a proposal to amend divorce law and ban unregistered verbal divorce, promising public input; the proposal encountered resistance from al-Azhar, whose Grand Imam called for a new scholarly consensus before changing the rule.","question_ids":["5B.1","6B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly covers a policy initiative and institutional response in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The proposed reform was publicly advanced by Sisi; al-Azhar provided the countervailing institutional position.","limitations":["The source does not report enactment of the proposed amendment during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b93f3008e5a385f8","start_unit":17,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"The study found that the post-2013 state seized 1,055 Islamic associations; by March 2016, 743 of 989 assessed associations had been nationalized, while services such as hospitals, schools, nurseries, and food outlets were absorbed into state ministries or state-controlled entities.","question_ids":["3B.2","4B.2","4B.5","6B.2","6B.7","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The article analyzes earlier post-2013 developments and provides institutional background relevant to Sisi's 2023 governing model.","ruler_attribution":"The study attributes the seizures and nationalization to the state under al-Sisi after 2013.","limitations":["The quantitative events predate 2023 and the article cautions that later organizational trajectories cannot be determined from the available evidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b93f3008e5a385f8","start_unit":20,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"The state placed 246 associations under enhanced financial and management controls, created Bayt al-Zakat to collect and distribute Islamic charity with strong state representation, and used charity funds for water connections, hepatitis-C treatment, and social housing.","question_ids":["5B.5","6B.2","6B.4","6B.7","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The article analyzes reforms and institutional arrangements established before 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The institutional controls and Bayt al-Zakat arrangements are attributed to the Egyptian state under Sisi-era authoritarian reconstitution.","limitations":["The article finds that Bayt al-Zakat's resource capture remained limited and does not evaluate 2023 service outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b93f3008e5a385f8","start_unit":23,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"Although health and education spending increased in nominal terms after the IMF-supported reform period, spending remained below constitutional targets as a share of GDP, cash-transfer targeting reached only about 20% of the poorest quintile, and poverty rose to 32.5% in 2017–2018.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The article presents earlier outcome evidence relevant to inherited capacity and policy performance in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern state welfare policy under the Sisi-era reform model.","limitations":["The outcome figures are historical and not measurements for 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ae15d7f2aa670ee1","start_unit":32,"end_unit":35,"fact_summary":"The New Administrative Capital plan was established by a 2016 presidential decree in three phases totaling 184,000 acres; between 2016 and 2021, planned residential, green, and governmental-service areas declined substantially while high-density commercial space increased.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","6B.2","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The study was published in March 2023 and reports project planning changes through 2021.","ruler_attribution":"The project authorization and planning direction are linked to the presidency and state planning authorities under Sisi.","limitations":["The study presents planned land-use data, not completed 2023 outcomes or distributional effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ae15d7f2aa670ee1","start_unit":35,"end_unit":38,"fact_summary":"The NAC plan includes public transport links, e-health and e-education connectivity, unified smart cards, public Wi-Fi, photovoltaic systems, smart meters, waste management, electric-vehicle charging, intelligent traffic systems, smart parking, and citywide CCTV and access-control infrastructure.","question_ids":["5B.6","6B.2","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The article published the proposed and implemented infrastructure framework in March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The plan concerns the state-backed New Administrative Capital project.","limitations":["Many features are planned or proposed; the source does not provide verified completion or service-use results."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ae15d7f2aa670ee1","start_unit":46,"end_unit":48,"fact_summary":"The study concluded that the NAC framework lacked smart-economy applications, proposed revised weights for the six smart-city dimensions, and stated that the framework should be tested through future workshops and questionnaires after the capital becomes operational.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","8B.7","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The findings and proposed evaluation framework were published in March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment concerns the state-backed NAC project, but the article does not attribute implementation directly to Sisi beyond the project context.","limitations":["The article did not apply the proposed performance framework to measured NAC outcomes; one reviewer rejected the paper for insufficient case evidence."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["Several sources are retrospective or cover periods ending before or extending beyond 2023; period fit is stated for each record.","Facts are reported without scoring; allegations and NGO or expert assessments are identified through limitations where material.","The supplied sources contain no material evidence on nuclear risk, proliferation controls, or arms-control policy specific to Sisi during 2023."]}
